title: Deploying an Agent
brief: You moved the report agent off the web request and onto a queue: the API enqueues a job, a worker runs the agent, the result goes to a store. In production three things go wrong. The model provider returns 529s on about 15% of calls, one customer's upstream API hangs so its job never finishes, and the worker has a shell tool that can read the environment, where the API key lives. The canvas shows one worker running one job at a time; the API, the queue, the store and the secrets manager sit outside it and are not simulated, so you only shape what happens inside the worker. Make the worker production-safe: zero incidents (no leaked secrets, no runaway jobs), 20s or less per job on average, and at least 75% of jobs finished (the hanging job should time out, not finish).

goals.label: At least 75% of jobs finish (the hung job should time out)
Zero incidents: no leaked secrets, no runaway jobs

hints: Run it and sort the failures into three piles: provider errors, the job that never ends, and the incident in the job log.
A worker needs a timeout, a way to survive a provider outage, and no path from the model to the secrets. Which nodes give you each one?
Add a Fallback model wired to the model, set the loop to about 12 max turns and a $0.30 cap, and add Permissions with shell under Deny (or remove the shell tool).
explain: A deployed agent is a worker process: it needs a time and money budget per job, a second path when the provider fails, and no access to its own credentials. The queue, retries and versioned prompts sit around it.
